title: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
section_text: The case concerned whether privacy is protected as a fundamental right.

title: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
section_text: Whether the right to privacy is protected under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

title: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
section_text: The petitioners argued that privacy is essential to life and personal liberty.

title: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
section_text: The Court examined earlier constitutional decisions and expanded the meaning of liberty. The Court followed Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) 1 SCC 248 and relied upon A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras AIR 1950 SC 27.

title: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
section_text: The Supreme Court held that the right to privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21.

title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
section_text: The petitioner challenged the impounding of her passport.

title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
section_text: Whether procedure established by law under Article 21 must be fair, just, and reasonable.

title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
section_text: The petitioner argued that personal liberty cannot be restricted by arbitrary procedure.

title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
section_text: The Court expanded the interpretation of Article 21.

title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
section_text: The Court held that any law affecting personal liberty must be fair, just, and reasonable.

title: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
section_text: The petitioner argued that detention affected personal liberty.
